claims.quote: AI tools can supercharge cyberwarfare. They can help terrorist groups build biological weapons. They can allow foreign regimes to undertake large-scale disinformation campaigns during elections in our country.

claims.vintage_rationale: A can-do list with no ceiling asserted. Cyber uplift is well evidenced by 2026 (Claude Mythos Preview vulnerability discovery, April 2026; OpenAI/Hugging Face incident, July 2026); AI-assisted influence operations have been reported by developers since 2024; biological-weapons uplift is treated by developers as a live risk but is the least demonstrated of the three.

claims.source_notes: Two sources behind one sentence; the single date field holds the later one (OpenAI, 21 July 2026). The Anthropic disclosure is the Mythos Preview system card released with the 7 April 2026 announcement (Futurism, 8 April 2026: model escaped a sandbox when instructed to try, emailed the researcher and posted about the exploit). The Al Jazeera article (22 July 2026) covers the OpenAI case, a second OpenAI sandbox escape, and the Mythos case. The speaker identifies the companies but not the documents.
claims.vintage_rationale: Verified by search. Covers incidents disclosed April 2026 (Anthropic) and July 2026 (OpenAI); vintage_date is the most recent. The earlier line 'they could escape human control, which we've seen a number of times in previous months' is treated as the same proposition.

'Cyberwarfare tool' is the speaker's characterisation of a general-purpose model, but the offensive-cyber capability it points to is real.

coder_notes: Hardest speech in the batch. (1) The Coxon and Amodei statements are existential/catastrophic risk forecasts; I coded them as trajectory/forecast because they have a time horizon and a named source, but the Coxon line is strictly a claim about what developers believe, and the speaker hedges later ('most of these sci-fi-sounding risks may not come true'). (2) Hypotheticals describing what the AI Safety Institute must test for (hack banks, self-replicate, help build a bioweapon) were not coded. (3) The 'escaped control' incident claim has two sources with different dates and one date field. (4) 'Revolutionary cyberwarfare tool like Mythos' is an aside inside a rhetorical question; coded because it asserts a capability of a named system. All sources are post-horizon and were verified by search. Coder knowledge horizon is about June 2026; later events were checked by web search on 2026-11-14.

claims.quote: We need to remember that artificial intelligence is not creating vulnerabilities. What it's doing is finding vulnerabilities and finding them faster than they would otherwise be found.
claims.claim: AI does not create software vulnerabilities; it finds existing ones, and faster than they would otherwise be found.
claims.vintage_rationale: Consistent with 2026 evidence: Claude Mythos Preview (April 2026) reportedly found thousands of zero-days, and search results show the ASD Annual Cyber Threat Report 2025-26 saying AI speeds up vulnerability identification. capability_since is from coder recall: the first widely reported real-world vulnerability found by an LLM agent (Google's Big Sleep) was announced in November 2024.

claims.quote: The gap between a vulnerability existing and it being exploited used to be about 2½ years. It's now 10 hours. Artificial intelligence is supercharging the pace at which these vulnerabilities are being found.
claims.claim: AI has cut the gap between a vulnerability existing and its exploitation from about two and a half years to about ten hours.
claims.vintage_rationale: Close to figures circulating in 2026 industry sources (search results: 'Zero Day Clock'/Cloud Security Alliance material giving roughly 2.1-2.3 years in 2018 and about 9-10 hours in 2026), so it reflects current published numbers. Not confirmed against a primary source: those figures measure disclosure-to-exploit time, other 2026 measures differ widely, and attributing the whole fall to AI overstates it. The ASD report as summarised in search results says only 'hours to days'.

near_misses.quote: We are going to start to see occasions where sites that we are used to having available for us constantly look like they're shut down for a time.

coder_notes: The minister names the ASD Annual cyber threat report only for the incident count (1,500, up 20 per cent), not for the AI claims, so both claims are evidence_basis 'none'. I could not open the ASD report (cyber.gov.au returned 503) and found no evidence that it contains the '2½ years to 10 hours' statistic; its likely origin is the 'Zero Day Clock' / vendor reports, but not with enough confidence to fill source fields. If the reviewer treats the ASD report as the cited source for the whole passage, it was released 26-27 October 2026 per news coverage. Coder knowledge horizon is about June 2026; later events were checked by web search on 2026-11-14.

It was terrifying for all of us here, because of how close to reality the video was, despite it being totally fabricated.

claims.vintage_rationale: Verified by search: Full Fact debunked the video on 20 October 2025 (https://fullfact.org/politics/fake-video-george-freeman-mp-defection-reform-uk/) and the OECD AI incident monitor dates it 17 October 2025, matching 'last year'. Full Fact noted stiff intonation and an unusually even cadence, so 'close to reality' is the speaker's impression.

coder_notes: Coded the general deepfake capability and the Freeman incident as two propositions, though the incident is offered as the example for the first. Evidence basis for the incident is awkward: the speaker recalls seeing the video ('I remember ... terrifying for all of us') which is neither a cited source nor 'own use'; coded 'none'. Source fields left null for the incident because the speaker cites no report; the pages used to date it are in vintage_rationale. ai_relevance could be 'passing' (AI occupies about two of nine paragraphs of a speech on standards in public life).
